messages:
Dev Patel: Dropping recurring Private customer pain points here (last ~6 weeks) so we can feed the “Private observability minimum pack” reqs. This is across VPC + on-prem.

Top themes:
1) “We installed Private but have no baseline dashboards” (or dashboards exist but are random / not the ones support asks for)
2) Alert thresholds are unclear / customers don’t know what to page on vs ticket
3) Log forwarding defaults are either too chatty or dropping (esp on-prem -> SIEM)
4) Prom rule loading / Grafana provisioning issues after upgrades

Concrete examples / tickets:
- SUP-2419: customer asked for latency dashboard + recommended panels/thresholds. They had Grafana but nothing about p95/p99, no breakdown prefill vs decode, no route/model segmentation.
- SUP-2431: “Alert rules not loading after upgrade” → promtool errors, customer thought alerts were active but they weren’t. We only found out once they had an outage.
- SUP-2427: on-prem logs dropping on the way to SIEM; they tweaked Fluent Bit and ended up with huge CPU + still missing error logs.
- INT-1184: internal staging env Grafana provisioning failing due to RBAC (same class of issue customers hit).
- INT-1190: multiple asks from Solutions/Support for a standard “supported signals” checklist.

What Support keeps asking customers for in triage (and they rarely have it ready):
- Gateway: RPS, 4xx/5xx, p50/p95/p99 latency, streaming disconnects
- Runtime: prefill vs decode latency, queue depth, batch sizes, KV cache hit rate (or equivalent)
- Saturation: GPU util/mem, throttling/thermal, node CPU/mem
- Control plane: config/policy store health, auth integration errors
- Installer/upgrade health: did the last upgrade apply cleanly? any components crashlooping?

Big friction: thresholds. Customers ask “is p95 1.5s bad?” and we end up hand-waving because we don’t have a default SLO + burn alert story for Private.

If the min pack can define:
- baseline dashboards (names + what they answer)
- baseline alerts with severity + default thresholds + tuning guidance
- a validation checklist (“supported install”) we can request in every case
…we’ll shave a lot of time off escalations.

:thread: please reply with any patterns you’ve seen + anything you think is a MUST for day-1 supportability.

Owen Phillips: +1 to all of this. Another common thing: customers *think* they have metrics because Prometheus is up, but half the targets are down / scraping wrong endpoints. We don’t notice until we ask for a graph and it’s empty.

Also: inconsistent metric labels across installs. Sometimes we get `model` label, sometimes it’s `model_name`, sometimes nothing. Makes it impossible to give customers copy/paste queries.

Re: thresholds — customers specifically ask for “when should I page for latency vs error rate vs saturation.” Right now we say “depends” and then they tune themselves into alert fatigue.

Liam O'Rourke: From TAM side, regulated enterprise prospects always ask for:
- audit trail for dashboard / alert rule changes (who changed what)
- retention guidance (what’s default vs what they must configure)
- how to forward logs to SIEM without exfil’ing sensitive prompt content
They get nervous when we say “bring your own dashboards.” They want something we support.

Markus Klein: This matches what we see on installs. For on-prem specifically, “no egress” trips up anything that assumes pulling dashboards/plugins at runtime.

We’ve had a few customers where Grafana is customer-managed and they don’t want us to touch it. So we need a mode where we ship dashboards as JSON + provisioning instructions, not only “installer provisions it for you.”

Also, upgrading: if a new pack version changes rule names/labels it breaks their silences and routing. We need versioning + migration notes.

Allison Grant: On the thresholds / SLO front: we should pick defaults that are about *burn-rate* rather than fixed p99 thresholds, otherwise it’s constant tuning per workload.

Support req I’d like to encode: “missing signals” alert group. If the gateway request counter is flat zero / scrape failures / rules not loaded, that should page (or at least warn) because it blocks diagnosis.

Elliot Price: For docs info architecture: please keep a single “If Support asks you for X, here’s where to find it” section. That’s what operators want under pressure.

If you have exact phrasing customers used (confusion points), paste here — we can mirror it in the install guide and runbook.

Kira Thompson: Re recurring confusion: customers don’t know what “prefill” vs “decode” means. We should define it *in the dashboard* (panel descriptions) + in the runbook.

Also, when rule loading fails (SUP-2431 pattern), customers need a deterministic check:
- `promtool check rules` equivalent
- confirm Prometheus actually has the `PrometheusRule` objects (if kube-prom stack)
- confirm Alertmanager is receiving alerts
We should include commands + expected output.

Sean Gallagher: For paging policy: please default to 2 severities only (page vs ticket) for the min pack. If we ship 4 severity levels customers won’t implement it.

Suggest:
- Page: availability SLO burn, high 5xx, “no metrics / no logs / rules not loaded,” GPU exhaustion imminent
- Ticket: elevated p95 latency (non-burn), high 4xx, capacity nearing limits, log drops (if partial)

Also: please bake in recommended inhibition rules (e.g., if Prometheus down, don’t page for every target down).

Dev Patel: This is super helpful. Summarizing Support “MUSTs” for requirements list:
- Dashboards shipped by default (gateway, runtime prefill/decode, saturation, control plane, installer health)
- Queries/panels must be copy/pasteable across installs → metric naming + label schema consistency
- Default SLO + burn-rate alerts for Private, with simple page vs ticket mapping
- “Missing signals / rules not loaded” detection to avoid silent failure of observability
- Log pipeline defaults with clear sampling + redaction guidance, and on-prem SIEM forwarding path that doesn’t melt nodes
- Docs: operator-friendly “Support asks for X” section + glossary (prefill/decode)

I’ll link this thread into PM-612/ENG-2848/ENG-2852. If anyone has additional ticket IDs or screenshots of empty dashboards / confusing alerts, DM me.

Owen Phillips: Adding one more: customers want a single “go-live validation” they can run and attach to a support ticket. Even a text report saying pass/fail on the basic signals would be huge.

Markus Klein: +1. We already do this ad-hoc in Solutions. If installer can output a post-install report (endpoints reachable, dashboards imported, rules loaded), that’s basically the definition of “supported.”

Dev Patel: :thumbsup: got it — will call out explicitly as a deliverable (post-install validation report).
